tweets.body: Interestingly, it is briefly depleted from Polycomb targets specifically in grown oocytes (its significance still unclear). Loss of H2A.Z impairs meiosis gene expression and oocyte maturation, ultimately causing female infertility.

tweets.body: Histone variant H2A.Z, which may be perfectly suited for gene regulation in oocytes which lack DNA replication, is installed at active promoters and enhancers, where it is widely acetylated and promotes regulatory activities.

tweets.title: Final model: strong enhancers near Xist not only jumpstart Xist in early embryos, but also bring cohesin which insulates enhancer activities to local regions. T
tweets.body: Final model: strong enhancers near Xist not only jumpstart Xist in early embryos, but also bring cohesin which insulates enhancer activities to local regions. This achieves an intricate balance on chrX between expression of essential genes and chromosome-wide silencing.

tweets.title: Loss of cohesin or the Xist regulatory region not only disrupts X-megadomains, but also causes ectopic enhancer activation and gene derepression near Xist.
tweets.body: Loss of cohesin or the Xist regulatory region not only disrupts X-megadomains, but also causes ectopic enhancer activation and gene derepression near Xist.

tweets.title: X-megadomains are specific to early development and correlate with strong enhancer activities near Xist. X-megadomains require cohesin, a regulatory region of X
tweets.body: X-megadomains are specific to early development and correlate with strong enhancer activities near Xist. X-megadomains require cohesin, a regulatory region of Xist with strong enhancers, as well as Xist expression.

tweets.title: Using Hi-C, we found a new configuration - megadomains hinged at the Xist region on the inactive X chromosome (termed X-megadomains) in mouse embryos. DXZ4-hing
tweets.body: Using Hi-C, we found a new configuration - megadomains hinged at the Xist region on the inactive X chromosome (termed X-megadomains) in mouse embryos. DXZ4-hinged megadomains occurred later and surprisingly in a strain-specific manner due to loss of DXZ4 repeats in some strains.
